help.sub: Every number here is free to call. You do not have to be in trouble to use them.
help.title: Free help in Hong Kong
help.unreviewed: No life in this game has been reviewed yet by the community it is about. The figures are an illustration.
helpLine.anti-scam.note: This line is for advice. To report a crime, go to a police station. In an emergency, call 999.
helpLine.anti-scam.what: Call this free number if you think someone is trying to trick you out of your money. A police officer will talk it through with you.
helpLine.basic-housing.note: District teams near you can help a tenant in person. They are listed on the same site.
helpLine.basic-housing.what: Ask the government whether your flat meets the rules on size, window, toilet and ceiling. This line is about the flat itself, not about the rent.
helpLine.caritas-debt.note: Their family crisis line is 18288, also day and night.
helpLine.caritas-debt.what: Free help from a social worker if you owe money you cannot pay back. They explain your choices and help you make a plan.
helpLine.cheer.note: They translate free of charge in Tagalog, Bahasa Indonesia, Urdu, Nepali, Hindi, Punjabi, Thai and Vietnamese.
helpLine.cheer.what: A free centre for people from ethnic minority communities. They give advice, help you deal with government offices, and translate for you on the phone.
helpLine.eaa.note: You can complain in Tagalog, Bahasa Indonesia, Thai or Khmer on their online form.
helpLine.eaa.what: Free government help if an employment agency overcharges you or lies to you. An agency may charge you no more than one tenth of your first month's pay.
helpLine.enrich.note: 5981 3754 for English and Tagalog. 5648 0990 for Bahasa Indonesia.
helpLine.enrich.what: Free money classes for migrant domestic workers. How to save, how to spot a loan trap, and how to plan for going home.
helpLine.eoc.what: Free help if someone treats you unfairly because of your race, your sex, a disability or your family. At work, at school, or when renting a home.
helpLine.labour-fdh.note: If you are in danger, call 999.
helpLine.labour-fdh.what: Free government help about your job. Your pay, your rest days, your contract, or an agency that treats you badly.
helpLine.labour-general.note: The call is answered by the government's 1823 call centre.
helpLine.labour-general.what: Free government help about any job in Hong Kong. Ask about your pay, your hours, your rest days, or being dismissed.
helpLine.rvd-tenancy.note: This is the line for rent, deposit and electricity charges. Their own page tells you to call the interpretation line first if you need another language.
helpLine.rvd-tenancy.what: Free government help about the rent on a subdivided flat. They check what your landlord is allowed to charge, and you can report a landlord who charges too much.
helpLine.scameter.note: The phone app is called Scameter+. The website is in English and Chinese only.
helpLine.scameter.what: A free police website. Type in a phone number, a website or a bank account. It tells you if people have reported it as a scam.
helpLine.twghs-debt.hours: Monday to Friday, 10am to 1pm and 2pm to 6pm. Also Friday 7pm to 10pm.
helpLine.twghs-debt.note: They give advice only. They do not apply for bankruptcy or a repayment plan for you.
helpLine.twghs-debt.what: Free help from a counsellor if you owe money. They go through what you owe and help you decide what to pay first.
